protocol_checks.vulnerability_mechanism: CONFIRMED: at e167299f6050d85778e62ed2a1e544ceef6452fc, REQUEST only casts client->requestBuffer. ProcXFixesSetClientDisconnectMode then reads stuff->disconnect_mode without REQUEST_SIZE_MATCH, while the swapped path permits REQUEST_AT_LEAST_SIZE. A short request can therefore consume residual request-buffer bytes, store them as the disconnect mode, and the sibling Get handler returns that stored value. The current PUBLISHED CVE record and the 2025-06-17 X.Org advisory describe this same prior-request data leak.
protocol_checks.atomic_bic: CONFIRMED: git log --all --reverse -S over both ProcXFixesSetClientDisconnectMode and its vulnerable assignment identifies e167299f6050d85778e62ed2a1e544ceef6452fc as the sole first write. Its new xfixes/disconnect.c contains the live dispatch handler and missing exact-size check; no earlier public commit in the assigned clone writes the vulnerable lines. It is the smallest surviving public Git object for the first write.
protocol_checks.immediate_parent_absence: CONFIRMED: the BIC has exactly one parent, b7a85e44da91d1663d5b4eabac06327c92a80f91. That parent has no xfixes/disconnect.c and git grep finds no SetClientDisconnectMode, ClientDisconnectMode, or ProcXFixesSetClientDisconnectMode symbol, proving absence of the vulnerable handler rather than merely absence of the later fix.
